description:
FILED s473t3 (Opus triage of the 79 CATALOG-only blessed rows), on main
d9a2aac0.  PRE-EXISTING.  Probe: scratch/s473t3/probes/p07-arylen-freed.pl.

ROWS BEHIND IT (baselines/fail-baseline.tsv, 6 rows):
  array.t 83 `$a: $# on freed array is undef`
  array.t 84 `$a: number of warnings`
  array.t 85 `$a: msg`
  array.t 86 `do {}: $# on freed array is undef`
  array.t 87 `do {}: number of warnings`
  array.t 88 `do {}: msg`

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl):
    print "stack_refcounted=", Internals::stack_refcounted(), "\n";
    my $a = \$#{[]};
    print "deref=", (defined $$a ? "[$$a]" : "undef"), "\n";
    my @warn; local $SIG{__WARN__} = sub { push @warn, "@_" };
    local $^W = 1;
    $$a = 1000;
    print "nwarn=", scalar(@warn), " first=", ($warn[0] // "none"), "\n";
    my $b = do { my @x; \$#x };
    print "do-deref=", (defined $$b ? "[$$b]" : "undef"), "\n";
  perl: stack_refcounted=0
        deref=undef
        nwarn=1 first=Attempt to set length of freed array at ... line 7.
        do-deref=undef
  PCL : stack_refcounted=0
        deref=[-1]
        nwarn=0 first=none
        do-deref=[-1]
  (`Internals::stack_refcounted()` is 0 in BOTH, so the test takes its
  non-RC branch on both sides -- the divergence is not the internals stub.)

MECHANISM: the `p-magic-cell` that backs `\$#array` (session 218) closes over
the VECTOR with a strong reference, so the temporary array can never die.
perl frees it as soon as the statement ends, leaves the magic pointing at a
dead AV, and reports undef / warns on a write.  Fixing it needs
`sb-ext:make-weak-pointer` plus GC determinism -- the same family as
DESTROY-via-GC.  Fix area: `p-arylen-ref` in `cl/pcl-runtime.lisp`.

CATALOG NOTE THIS REPLACES: sweep-bug-catalog.md array.t, "freed-array
(83-88, 100): the GC-hard corner ... the magic cell holds a *strong* ref to
the vector so it never dies.  Leave."  The prediction is CONFIRMED here with
a standalone reproducer.

FAMILY: GC-observable lifetime, alongside `docs/not-supported.md`
"`DESTROY` called by garbage collector".  This one is NOT registered there
because the arylen cell's strong reference is PCL's own choice, not the GC's
nondeterminism.
subject: BUG (arylen magic): `\$#{[]}` keeps the temporary array ALIVE, so `$$ref` reads -1 where perl reads undef and a write succeeds silently where perl warns "Attempt to set length of freed array"
